Bug_Title: ICAST: int value cast to float and then passed to Math.round (ICAST_INT_CAST_TO_FLOAT_PASSED_TO_ROUND)
Bug_Details:
This code converts an int value to a float precision
floating point number and then
passing the result to the Math.round() function, which returns the int/long closest
to the argument. This operation should always be a no-op,
since converting an integer to a float should give a number with no fractional part.
It is likely that the operation that generated the value to be passed
to Math.round was intended to be performed using
floating point arithmetic.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where an integer value is first cast to a float and then passed to Math.round. This operation is unnecessary because casting an int to a float does not introduce any fractional part, making the subsequent Math.round call redundant.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with various integer values. The bug is present in the showBug method where an integer value is first cast to a float and then passed to Math.round. This operation is unnecessary because casting an int to a float does not introduce any fractional part, making the subsequent Math.round call redundant. The test case 'testShowBugWithFailingCase' is designed to fail, thereby triggering the bug.
